owner: TEACHER (stock_decision_v1/teacher/sdv1_failure_ledger.py reads it); PILOT-DATA adopts it in sd0_render.py
why: REVIEW_2026-10-13_2105 finding 4: sd0_render copied label_basis (a provenance term) into both target_basis and label_verification; the failure ledger used a different vocabulary, so rule_oracle / human_annotation gold with every teacher wrong came out ambiguous_or_defective_label instead of common_teacher_failure.

fields.target_basis: WHAT the gold distribution means (a key of target_basis below). Decides hard vs soft scoring.
fields.label_verification: HOW the gold's correctness was established (a key of label_verification below). Decides whether a model disagreement can be a failure category or must be a review item.
fields.label_provenance: WHERE the label came from upstream: the Stage 0 source-map label_basis value, verbatim (a key of stage0_provenance_map). Never used as target_basis or label_verification directly.
fields.label_provenance_detail: optional free text (source-map reason, recast id, review id)
fields.evidence_refs: list of references that establish the label: source record ids, oracle / rule ids + revisions, execution fixture ids, review ids, cited spans. [] when none is available (allowed; recorded as such).

optimal_action.distribution: one-hot over actions (the Bayes action under a stated loss)
optimal_action.native_metric: action_regret when loss_by_option is given, else tie_accepting_hard_accuracy

realised_outcome.distribution: one-hot: the outcome that actually happened (court ruling, AfD close, trial result ...)
realised_outcome.note: an aleatoric event: a wrong argmax is not by itself a reasoning error; failure categories are kept but generation_priority becomes 'review'

recorded_action.distribution: one-hot: what a recorded agent / person did

exact_posterior.distribution: exact posterior / posterior-predictive of a stated model

outcome_probability.distribution: probability of a future outcome from a stated process

graded_rating.distribution: ordinal human rating: one level, or a soft interpolation between neighbouring levels
graded_rating.native_metric: hard if the gold is one-hot or a uniform tie set, else soft_metrics

hardness_rule: scoring 'from_gold': hard when the nonzero gold entries are all equal (one-hot, or uniform over a set of equally correct keys: tie-accepting accuracy); soft when they differ (graded relevance, annotator splits, interpolated ratings). A soft row is never a failure category (soft_target_metric_only: NLL / Brier stored; a verified failure needs evidence).

exact_oracle.means: an owned, versioned executable rule / exact calculation produced the label

execution_check.means: the label was established by executing code / tests

construction_rule.means: the label is fixed by the generating template's construction (e.g. BBQ, HANS)

outcome_record.means: the label is the recorded outcome from an authoritative record

retained_human_distribution.means: the observed annotator distribution, kept as collected

cited_evidence_review.means: cited evidence + an independent review (DATA_SPEC accepted class)

checked_teacher_reasoning.means: teacher reasoning independently checked (DATA_SPEC accepted class)

author_constructed.means: written with a unique answer by its author (the teacher dry-run set only)

source_human_gold.means: the curated human gold label of the source dataset, not re-verified by us (annotation noise possible)

upstream_llm_reviewed.means: an upstream label whose recast was reviewed by an LLM (tasksource GLM-5.3 review): NOT independent verification

model_label.means: the label was produced by a model

unaudited_rule.means: a generator rule without an independent audit

recorded_behaviour.means: what an agent did; says nothing about correctness

tiers.independent: accepted: model / gold disagreements are failure categories
tiers.source_gold: accepted as gold for categorisation (standard dataset gold); errors possible
tiers.unverified: NOT accepted: any model disagreement with the gold -> ambiguous_or_defective_label (a review item); a per-source independent audit (DATA_SPEC 50-example family QC) may promote a source via promotions below

always: common_teacher_failure always carries needs_independent_check = true (an executable oracle or two independent grounded reviews before it may be called a teacher error), whatever the tier.

upstream_annotation_llm_reviewed.note: soft tasksource rows (source_label_soft: annotator disagreement or interpolated ratings) score soft by the hardness rule

unit_target_basis_aliases.note: tasksource unit-level curation target_basis (convert_tasksource_ff.py); it never overrides the provenance mapping

renderer_contract.label_verification: stage0_provenance_map[label_basis].label_verification (a per-row verified value, when one exists, wins)
renderer_contract.label_provenance_detail: the source-map reason / recast id when available
renderer_contract.evidence_refs: source record id, oracle / rule id + revision, review id when available; [] otherwise

resolution_in_the_ledger: 1. A value of label_verification or target_basis that is a stage0_provenance_map key is mapped through it (covers rows rendered before this schema, where both fields hold label_basis).
2. Otherwise each field is read from its own table (ledger_v1_aliases accepted).
3. Unknown verification -> tier unverified; unknown target basis -> hardness from the gold and flagged unknown_target_basis.
revision_note: 2026-10-14 r2: (1) hardness_rule: a uniform tie set over equally correct keys is HARD (tie-accepting); (2) every one-hot-type basis (hard_fact, optimal_action, realised_outcome, recorded_action) scores 'from_gold', so a graded gold under such a basis (e.g. per-question overrides of realised_outcome rows) is soft, never a failure category. stage0_provenance_map target / verification values, tiers, fields and renderer contract are unchanged from r1 (md5 7cf436b2).
